units.label: Abstract
units.text: Names the battery and announces the results: mixed-state conversions become reversible under LOCC with a battery; the asymptotic rate is a ratio of entanglement; different quantifiers give different second laws.

units.label: Introduction

units.label: Asymptotic transformations of entangled states and reversibility

units.label: Reversible manipulations with a battery: the setting
units.text: The transformation ρ⊗τ → σ⊗τ~ and the battery condition E(τ~) ≥ E(τ) define the operation class; the required properties of E are listed.

units.label: Theorem 1
units.text: Theorem 1 is stated with an outline of its proof (monotonicity for necessity, a swap with the battery for sufficiency).

units.label: Theorem 2 and reversibility
units.text: Theorem 2 is stated with an outline; R(ρ→σ)·R(σ→ρ) = 1 is concluded from it.

units.label: Quantifiers that qualify
units.text: Squashed entanglement is named as a quantifier with the required properties; the regularised relative entropy and logarithmic negativity are discussed; multipartite extension.

units.label: Relation to Ref. [7]; correlations; geometric entanglement
units.text: The result is contrasted with the no-go of Ref. [7] (the operation may depend on the initial and final states); entanglement cannot be created from separable states; geometric entanglement does not constrain conversions.

units.label: Quantum thermodynamics
units.text: Free energy and the free-energy battery; Theorem 3 is stated.

units.label: Conclusions
units.text: Summary and outlook; no new node or route.

units.label: Methods: LOCC with entanglement battery

units.label: Methods: proof of Theorem 1
units.text: Additivity (12) and asymptotic continuity (13) are written out; necessity by Eq. (14); sufficiency by the swap, Eqs. (15)–(17).

units.label: Methods: proof of Theorem 2
units.text: Upper bound on the rate, Eqs. (19)–(25); achievability by relabelling with a battery of copies, Eqs. (26)–(27).

units.label: Methods: proof of Theorem 3

units.label: Methods: zero-error conversion
units.text: The zero-error rate equals E(ρ)/E(σ) without asymptotic continuity.

units.label: Methods: measures that are additive and asymptotically continuous
units.text: Properties of squashed entanglement, each with its reference: additivity [27], faithfulness [31], asymptotic continuity [32].

units.label: Methods: other entanglement measures
units.text: Relative entropy of entanglement; logarithmic negativity is defined and said to allow PPT states from separable states.

nodes.title: Additivity of E (Eq. (12))
nodes.definition: E(ρ^{AB}⊗σ^{A'B'}) = E(ρ^{AB}) + E(σ^{A'B'}) for all states.

routes.statement: Definition of battery-assisted LOCC: the operation class is defined through the quantifier E.
If ρ → σ under battery-assisted LOCC then E(ρ) ≥ E(σ).
If E(ρ) ≥ E(σ) then ρ → σ: take τ = σ and swap A↔A', B↔B'; then τ~ = ρ.
ρ → σ under battery-assisted LOCC iff E(ρ) ≥ E(σ).
Zero-error rates satisfy m/n ≤ E(ρ)/E(σ).
Every pair (n, m) with m E(σ) ≤ n E(ρ) is achieved exactly by relabelling, with battery σ^{⊗m} → ρ^{⊗n}.
Rational rates m/n approach E(ρ)/E(σ) from below.
R_ze(ρ → σ) = E(ρ)/E(σ) for additive, monotone, finite E with E(σ) > 0.
With error ε: m/n ≤ (E(ρ) + f(ε)/n)/(E(σ) − g(ε) log2 d) whenever g(ε) log2 d < E(σ).
The bound of GB9 converges to E(ρ)/E(σ) as ε → 0.
routes.where: Eq. (25) and the sentence after it

routes.statement: R(ρ → σ) = E(ρ)/E(σ) for finite, additive, monotone, asymptotically continuous E.
E_sq is additive on tensor products and does not increase under LOCC.
E_sq(ρ) = 0 iff ρ is separable; E_sq is finite; E_sq of a pure state is the entropy of entanglement.
|E_sq(ρ) − E_sq(σ)| ≤ 16√(2ε) log d + 4h(2√(2ε)) for trace distance ≤ ε.
E_g(ψ_d^{⊗n}) = E_g(φ+^{⊗n}) = 1 − 2^{−n} while S(ψ_d^A) = 1 + ½ log2(d−1); E_g is not additive.
With E = E_g the battery condition permits φ+^{⊗n} → ψ_d^{⊗n} for every d, hence unbounded singlet yield.
Pure states are distilled to singlets by LOCC at rate S(ψ^A).
routes.where: Ref. [8], section on asymptotic transformations; used after Eq. (84)

routes.statement: ‖(|φ+><φ+|)^{T_A}‖₁ = 2; for σ_ε the trace norm is 1 + 2√(ε(1−ε)).
With error ε the singlet rate under the E_N battery obeys m/n ≤ E_N(ρ) − (1/n)log2(1−ε).
E_N is additive and LOCC monotone; ‖X^{T_A}‖₁ ≤ d_A‖X‖₁ (Eq. (76)).
(ρ,H) → (σ,H') with thermal operations and a free-energy battery iff F(ρ,H) ≥ F(σ,H').
F is additive over non-interacting systems, non-increasing under thermal operations, finite for 0 < T < ∞; swapping system and battery with their Hamiltonians is a thermal operation.
The states reachable from separable states are exactly those with E = 0.

units.label: Abstract
units.text: Recalls the claim that real-number quantum mechanics can be falsified; announces a real-number formulation that reproduces all multipartite predictions, and the conclusion that complex numbers are a matter of convenience.

units.label: Introduction
units.text: Earlier real formulations; Renou et al. [12] and the experiments; a locality requirement is proposed in place of the tensor-product postulate; the construction is announced as a quotient space in one-to-one correspondence with complex QM.

units.text: (P1)–(P3) as in Ref. [12]; (P4): operators of A act trivially on B and conversely.

units.label: Single system: the state map

units.label: Single system: operators and expectation values
units.text: T(Π), I_F and J_F; expectation values are preserved for single systems.

units.text: Same predictions as complex QM; the tensor-product postulate is criticised; complex numbers are not necessary but useful.

routes.statement: T: M_d(C) → M_2d(R) is an injective unital real-algebra homomorphism with T(A†) = T(A)^T, and its image is the commutant of Jd = 1⊗J.
S is real-linear and bijective C^d → R^2d with T(A)S(ψ) = S(Aψ), S(iψ) = Jd S(ψ), S(φ)^T S(ψ) = Re<φ|ψ>, S(φ)^T Jd S(ψ) = −Im<φ|ψ>, S(ψ)^T T(A) S(ψ) = Re<ψ|A|ψ>.
T1(ρ) = T(ρ)/2 has unit trace, tr[T1(ρ)T(A)] = Re tr(ρA), and A ≥ 0 ⇒ T(A) ≥ 0.
P = (1 − J⊗J)/2 is the orthogonal projector onto span{ψ_even^(2), ψ_odd^(2)}; its kernel is spanned by |00>+|11>, |01>−|10>; on its range J⊗1 = 1⊗J.
S(ψ)⊗_F S(φ) = R(ψ⊗φ): the class of S(ψ)⊗S(φ) has canonical representative R(ψ⊗φ)/√2, and Eq. (34) is R(ψ⊗φ).
ψ_even^(N) + iψ_odd^(N) = 2^{−(N−1)/2}(|0>+i|1>)^{⊗N}; J_k ψ_even = ψ_odd and J_k ψ_odd = −ψ_even for every flag k; the subspace on which all J_k agree is two-dimensional.
I^(N) is a projector, (J^(N))² = −I^(N); I^(N+M) = (I^(N)⊗I^(M) − J^(N)⊗J^(M))/2, J^(N+M) = (I^(N)⊗J^(M) + J^(N)⊗I^(M))/2; partial traces of I^(N), J^(N) are I^(N−M), J^(N−M).
(T(A)⊗1)R(Ψ) = R((A⊗1)Ψ) and (1⊗T(B))R(Ψ) = R((1⊗B)Ψ) for all A, B and all Ψ ∈ C^dA⊗C^dB.
T(A)⊗T(B) commutes with P and P(T(A)⊗T(B)) = Re(A⊗B)⊗I^(2) + Im(A⊗B)⊗J^(2) = ½[T(A)⊗T(B) − T(iA)⊗T(iB)].
R(Φ)^T [T(A)⊗T(B)] R(Ψ) = Re<Φ|A⊗B|Ψ>; hence all bipartite Born probabilities coincide with those of complex QT, entangled states included.
Complex QT with |φ+>_{AB1}|φ+>_{B2C}, A = (Z, X, Y), C = ((X±Z), (Y±Z), (X±Y))/√2 and Bob's Bell measurement gives P(b) = 1/4 and T = 6√2.
The real model with state |φ+>|φ+>|ψ_even^(4)> and operators T(Π^A)⊗T(Π^B)⊗T(Π^C) gives the same probabilities P(a,b,c|x,z) as complex QT for all outcomes and settings, hence T = 6√2.
The value 6√2 is obtained with the functional of Renou et al.; the form printed in the arXiv text (Eqs. (104)–(106), as extracted) differs in one sign prefactor and in the weighting.

units.label: Abstract
units.text: A decay is one fixed rotation-covariant measurement; single-setting data violate no Bell or steering inequality because the recorded directions are local hidden variables; the existence of a generalized-noncontextual model is decided exactly for spin 1/2 (P|κ| ≤ 1/3; ρ_raw and its partial transpose positive; ‖c‖₁ ≤ 1 and |D| ≤ 1/3), spin 1 (region R, pair region R₂, visibility 5/8) and spin j (ξ_2j, first-moment bound); muon and top decays, the ATLAS and CMS values of D and the BESIII ΛΛ̄ data; the results as routes of a concept graph.

units.text: Entanglement reported from decay angles; single-setting data admit a local model (the recorded momenta); a decay is a covariant POVM whose equivalent effects constrain a noncontextual model; noncontextuality is equivalent to simplex embeddability (Schmid et al.; Gitton and Woods; Selby et al.) and decidable by a linear programme (Selby et al.); the results (i)–(v) previewed with pointers; earlier work; the question read off as a missing connection between two released graphs.

units.text: Fragments, ontological models, noncontextuality; fragment-relative and quantum-relative equivalence; Lemma 1 (simplex embedding) with references, proof recalled in App. A; Remark 1: the recorded-outcome model is constructed, hence no Bell violation (Brunner et al.) and no steering (Wiseman et al.), and the example f = 3q_z² − 1 shows that it is not measurement noncontextual; Definition 2 (classical polarimeter).
